transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-01-19
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Redwood: Leah Park (AE), Marco Ruiz (SE), Nina Tran (CSM)
- Helios Biomed: Dr. Aisha Khan (Head of ML), Tom Bowers (Infra), Priya Rao (Security), Sofia Li (Procurement), Evan Milner (CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Helios wants to add dedicated capacity for EU production, run a private VPC pilot, and lock in a 12-month retainer. Security needs SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration notes. Procurement asked about invoicing cadence. Redwood to run targeted perf tests and provide SOW/pricing.

Topics covered:
1) Throughput/latency numbers and SLOs
2) Private VPC provisioning timeline
3) Pricing bands for committed retainer
4) Security/compliance artifacts and data residency

Action items (read back at end) included: benchmark run, SOW, PO cadence, security docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Leah Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um today we wanted to go through the retainer structure and the regional onramp for EU, make sure procurement and security have what they need.
[00:10] Dr. Aisha Khan: yep, thanks leah. we, uh, ran a quick internal Q&A, our main — main ask is predictable throughput for our customer-facing chat, we need p50 under 150ms for short chats, and p95 under 400ms ideally.
[00:26] Marco Ruiz: okay, that's helpful. are those numbers for the hosted API or for the private VPC?
[00:31] Dr. Aisha Khan: for production — so private VPC ideally, because of data residency. but we can acceptFallbacks for hosted during ramp, as long as the routing policy favors eu instances.
[00:44] Tom Bowers: just to add, our infra team's constraint is egress caps and a limited peering window, so we need to understand network patterns and egress charges.
[00:53] Leah Park: noted. Marco, can you talk briefly about how Redwood's smart routing and prefix caching would help preserve the latency budget while hitting cost targets?
[01:02] Marco Ruiz: sure, so two levers — caching for repeated prefixes which our runtime supports, and continuous batching on the serving layer. for short chats, batching is small but we use KV cache to avoid recomputing the prefix tokens. on private deployments the kernel selection and quantization profile also matter — we can tune for the customer workload. there might be some discrepancy in the numbers we see in hosted vs onprem though.
[01:28] Dr. Aisha Khan: when you say "tune" — like what are typical throughput numbers for a 1x A100-class node?
[01:33] Marco Ruiz: rough order of magnitude — using a mid-size open model, for short sequences you can see thousands of tokens per second with optimized kernels, but for the Helios prompt distribution we should run the benchmark. i'll run a 1k-token/sec sustained test on a private eu cluster to be concrete.
[01:49] Priya Rao: we will need KMS integration details — we use CloudVault HSM and our legal is strict about key custody. do you support customer-managed keys?
[01:58] Leah Park: yes, private deployments can use customer KMS/HSM, we have integrations notes. we'll send SOC2 artifacts and the KMS integration guide to priya.
[02:07] Priya Rao: ok please include any network diagram and the flow of logs — audit logs are critical.
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: quick note — audit logs for calls and model routing are available, but retention windows are configurable. there is a small overhead for long retention which might impact cost.
[02:22] Evan Milner: around costs — can you outline pricing for the retainer? we want three bands: baseline committed capacity, burst buffer, and on-demand overage.
[02:30] Leah Park: absolutely — our proposal will include 3 bands, and also a suggested quantization profile to hit lower unit costs. marcos will include perf numbers to match each band.
[02:41] Sofia Li: procurement question — invoicing cadence? quarter in advance or monthly?
[02:45] Leah Park: typically monthly billing for hosted customers, but for enterprise retainer we can do quarterly in advance with net-30. we'll write that in the SOW.
[02:54] Tom Bowers: i want to make sure the private pilot timeline lines up with our EU rollout — we have a code freeze on 2026-02-15, so ideally pilot is provisioned and smoke-tested by 02-10. is that workable?
[03:05] Marco Ruiz: tight but doable, we have a provisioning playbook — allocation, VPN peering, KMS handshake, and then a two-day ramp to run synthetic workloads. i'll map out a timeline and include it in the follow-up.
[03:16] Dr. Aisha Khan: and critical for us: what happens if the dedicated pool is saturated? we need graceful degradation to lower-cost model variants without failing the chat flow.
[03:26] Marco Ruiz: we support fallback policies: route to compatible model variant or to hosted pool. we can set priorities by route and customer tier. there is also an automatic canary rollback for model rollouts.
[03:36] Leah Park: good to flag that so you have a plan for outages.
[03:39] Priya Rao: security question — do you keep KV cache in memory only or persist cache to disk? we need to understand encryption at rest.
[03:46] Marco Ruiz: KV cache is typically memory-resident, but in some private setups we persist to encrypted storage to speed cold-starts. everything at rest can be encrypted with your KMS keys.
[03:56] Speaker 1: (mumbles) what about observability — do we get token-level cost showback?
[04:02] Nina Tran: yes we expose token-level cost and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console, you can set alerts on unit-cost regression.
[04:09] Leah Park: okay, i'd like to go through the timeline and next steps — leah speaking now — we'll do: run perf benchmark (marco), send SOW (leah), procurement follow-up (sofia), security artifacts (priya).
[04:20] Dr. Aisha Khan: sounds good. a couple of smaller items — does redwood support model pinning for canary? we need predictable behavior during rolling updates.
[04:29] Marco Ruiz: yes model pinning is supported; you can pin by version for a route and do canary percentages as well.
[04:34] Evan Milner: any gotchas on private deployments vs on-prem? like licensing or support tiers?
[04:39] Leah Park: private has a platform licensing fee and optional premium support for 24/7. for on-prem setups there's an additional engineering onboarding and runbook fee. we'll lay that out in the SOW.
[04:50] Tom Bowers: network diagram and egress estimate would be helpful for our finance team to prelim the cost of peering.
[04:57] Marco Ruiz: i'll include an expected egress profile and a small table of cost sensitivity for batching and quantization.
[05:04] Sofia Li: procurement want to know how we show usage — is there a CSV export or API?
[05:08] Nina Tran: both — we give usage reports, daily CSV exports and an API endpoint for programmatic retrieval.
[05:14] Dr. Aisha Khan: what about data retention policies for prompts? i.e., are prompts retained for training or just logs?
[05:21] Leah Park: by default we retain request logs for 90 days, you can opt-out of training data collection. private deployments respect your retention policy and logs location.
[05:29] Priya Rao: we'll need a written attestation for training opt-out for legal.
[05:34] Leah Park: we'll include that as a clause in the SOW and provide an attestation template.
[05:38] 
[30:12] (mid-call) Marco Ruiz: running through the benchmark plan — i'll provision a EU private cluster, mirror Helios prompt distribution sample, run two-week sustained test with peak bursts, capture p50/p95/p99 and token/sec. will also test fallback to hosted. i'll post results to the shared doc.
[30:31] Tom Bowers: what's the expected overhead for audit log retention at 1 year?
[30:36] Marco Ruiz: depends on volume; rough rule — logs are 2-4% of token cost if you retain raw transcripts for long windows. we'll quantify in the follow-up.
[30:43] Sofia Li: legal also asked about termination terms and data deletion SLA.
[30:48] Leah Park: standard termination with 30 days notice and data deletion within 60 days; for private deployments we can shorten that but we'd need to confirm operational steps.
[30:56] Evan Milner: okay, so to recap — leah will send SOW; marco will run perf and share benchmark sheet; priya will get security docs; sofia will coordinate procurement. any other items?
[31:06] Dr. Aisha Khan: one more — can we trial quantized model to reduce unit cost during the pilot?
[31:11] Marco Ruiz: yes, we can test 8-bit quantized path for the private pilot, quality checks against your eval prompts will be needed.
[31:19] Leah Park: perfect. we'll attach a short eval set and a regression alert in Redwood Optimize.
[31:24] 
[46:50] Leah Park: thanks everybody, we'll follow up with the SOW and the benchmark plan. last callouts — target dates: SOW 2026-01-22, perf results 2026-01-26, procurement update 2026-01-29. thanks and we'll talk next week.
[46:58] Dr. Aisha Khan: thanks, bye.

Questions noted in call:
- What are exact p50/p95 numbers per model variant?
- How disruptive is fallback routing when pool is saturated?
- Can we use our HSM with private deployment?
